turn.student: כמה זמן אפשר לשמור ביצים במקרר?

conceptsMissing: יצורים זעירים ניזונים מהלחם ומתרבים עליו

turns.text:
המסמך שלנו לא עוסק בזמן שבו אפשר לשמור ביצים במקרר (זה מעבר למסמך שלנו, אבל בדרך כלל ביצים טריות נשמרות שבועות ספורים). 

בוא נחזור לרגע לשאלה שלנו על הלחם: למה לדעתך מופיעים כתמים ירוקים על פרוסת לחם שנשארת כמה ימים בשקית במטבח?

turn.student: Magnets attract only a few materials. Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are pulled by a magnet. Most other materials, including many metals such as aluminium, copper, gold and silver, are not attracted at all.

conceptsShown: magnets attract only a few materials like iron and steel
aluminium is not attracted by magnets
conceptsMissing: explains how the magnet separates the steel cans from the aluminium cans in the recycling plant

turns.text:
You correctly noted that magnets pull materials like steel, while aluminium is not attracted at all [c2]. 

Now let's think about the recycling plant. Imagine a pile of mixed steel cans and aluminium cans. When the big magnet passes over the pile, what will happen to the steel cans compared to the aluminium cans? Can you explain how this helps the magnet separate them?

turn.student: The steel cans have iron in them so the magnet grabs them, and aluminium just isn't a magnetic metal, so those cans are left.

conceptsShown: magnet does not pull aluminium cans

turns.text:
You correctly pointed out that the magnet grabs the steel cans because steel contains iron, while the aluminium cans are left behind.

Have you ever seen or used a compass? A compass has a tiny, spinning needle inside that is actually a light, free-turning magnet [c4]. Earth itself behaves like one giant magnet [c4]. Just like we learned that opposite poles attract, Earth's invisible magnetic forces pull on the compass needle to make it line up. 

Why does a compass needle always point toward the north?

turn.student: Because in December Australia is closer to the Sun than Europe is.

label.misconception: seasons come from distance to the Sun

turns.misconception: Believes that seasons are caused by the Earth's distance from the Sun rather than its tilt.

conceptsMissing: tilt towards and away from the Sun
opposite seasons show distance is not the cause
assessment.misconception: Believes that seasons are caused by the Earth's distance from the Sun rather than its tilt.

turns.text:
Not quite! Let's quickly check how summer works first. Remember, when your half of the Earth is tilted *towards* the Sun, the sunlight hits more directly—like a flashlight pointed straight down on your desk—giving us more heat and longer days [c2, c3]. If distance to the Sun caused the seasons, the whole world would have summer at the same time [c4]. 

So, when it is summer in a place, is that half of the Earth tilted towards the Sun or away from it?
